name: Abu Bakr al-Siddiq
nameAr: عبد الله بن عثمان بن عامر بن عمرو بن كعب بن سعد بن تيم بن مرة التيمي، أبو بكر بن أبي قحافة، الصديق، رضي الله عنه
bornNote: two years and six months after the Year of the Elephant (al-Isabah, as given on the Shamela record)
role: First caliph; the Prophet's companion in the cave

companionCounts.source: Totals: al-Khazraji, Khulasat Tadhhib Tahdhib al-Kamal, p. 206 (142 hadith; 6 agreed upon; 11 in al-Bukhari alone; 1 in Muslim alone). In al-Bukhari: Ibn Hajar, Hady al-Sari, ch. 10 (22)

flags.label: Names and titles
flags.detail: Ibn Hajar surveys the explanations of Atiq (his original name; freedom from blemish in lineage; precedence in good; his beauty; his mother's prayer at his birth; the Prophet's good tidings that Allah freed him from the Fire, supported by Aishah's hadith in al-Tirmidhi and Ibn al-Zubayr's in al-Bazzar, which adds that his name before that was Abdullah ibn Uthman) and of al-Siddiq (his being first to affirm the Prophet ﷺ; or so named from the morning of the Night Journey; Ali swore that Allah sent the name down from heaven). Uthman is Abu Quhafah's name without dispute, as the kunya Abu Bakr is undisputed (Fath al-Bari on 3653).

bio: The first adult man to believe and the Prophet's companion in the migration and the cave, named the second of the two in al-Tawbah 9:40. He became the first caliph and died in 13 AH. His lineage meets the Prophet's at Murrah ibn Ka'b. He is known by his kunya, as was his father, Abu Quhafah; his own name was Abdullah. In hadith 4663 a Companion narrates from him: Anas reports Abu Bakr's own account of the cave.

provenance.ref: al-Isabah, as given on the Shamela record
Fath al-Bari on 3653 (opening of the merits of Abu Bakr)
